newsitem.title: GERMANY: Conti 96 sales seen up two pct-newsletter.
newsitem.headline: Conti 96 sales seen up two pct-newsletter.

text.p: German tyre giant Continental AG was expected to see 1996 sales climb two percent to 10.5 billion marks, a newsletter reported on Wednesday.

The Platow-Brief also said Continental's supervisory board would decide at an April 14 meeting whether to dismiss Klaus Roeker, the management board member responsible for the firm's truck tyre business.
Continental could not immediately be reached for comment.
For the first nine months of 1996, Continental sales rose 2.6 percent to 7.63 bilion marks, although truck tyre sales slumped 7.1 percent to 800 million marks under weak demand for heavy equipment.
Nine-month pre-tax profit rose 62 percent to 125 million marks, as Continental shifted some production out of Germany to lower-wage facilities in Ireland and the Czech Republic.
In November the company said it expected strong winter tyre sales to push fourth quarter results to match "very good levels" from 1995.
Continental last week said it would not sell a 50.1 percent stake in Benecke-Kaliko, reversing an earlier decision to unleash the car parts manufacturer.
